skill.name: skill-installer
skill.description: Lists and installs Codex skills from curated sources or GitHub repositories, with options for private repositories, refs, destinations, and download methods.
skill.summary: Install curated or repository-hosted Codex skills with configurable sources and destinations.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 20 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, expected GitHub URLs, documented installation paths, or token-name references. Two semantic risks remain: unverified installation from mutable remote sources and permission to overwrite preinstalled system skills. The package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced helper scripts were not available for review.

remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation, pin an immutable commit, display installed files, and verify a recorded content hash before writing.

remediation.issue: Preinstalled system skills may be overwritten.
remediation.suggestion: Prohibit changes to the system skill directory and require a separate administrator-controlled recovery process.

remediation.issue: Helper implementations are absent from the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced scripts and audit their credential handling, downloads, path validation, and archive extraction.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Remote Skill Installation
semantic_findings.description: The skill installs content from arbitrary GitHub repositories and defaults to mutable refs without requiring source review or integrity verification. Installed skills can persist untrusted instructions or executable content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 15 and 38-48 explicitly support arbitrary repository installation, direct downloads, and a default main ref.

semantic_findings.title: System Skill Overwrite Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits downloading and overwriting preinstalled system skills after user insistence. Replacing trusted system instructions can persist malicious behavior across later sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 55 directly permits overwriting preinstalled system skills, crossing the documented trust boundary.

content.value_statement: Installing skills manually requires choosing sources, authentication, and destination settings. This skill guides curated and GitHub installations through standard helper commands.
actual_capabilities: Lists curated skills and marks entries already installed.
Installs a curated skill by name.
Installs one or more skills from GitHub repository paths.
Accepts repository URLs, refs, destinations, and download method options.
Uses direct downloads for public repositories with sparse Git checkout fallback.
Supports private repositories through existing Git credentials or optional GitHub tokens.
limitations: Referenced helper scripts are not included in the audited package, so their implementation was not reviewed.
Repository refs default to mutable main branches unless the user supplies another ref.
The instructions do not require source verification or content integrity checks.
Installing skills changes instructions available to Codex after restart.

use_cases.title: Install a team skill

prompt_templates.title: List curated skills
prompt_templates.prompt: List the curated skills available from the default repository. Mark which skills are already installed.

prompt_templates.title: Install a curated skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Install the curated skill named [skill-name]. Confirm the source and destination before running the helper.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic installation from the curated collection.

prompt_templates.title: Install from GitHub
prompt_templates.prompt: Install the skill at [GitHub URL] using ref [commit SHA]. Review the source and show the destination before installation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate installation from a public repository.

prompt_templates.title: Install multiple private skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Install [path one] and [path two] from [owner/repository] at [commit SHA]. Use existing credentials, destination [path], and the git method.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced private repository installation with explicit controls.

output_examples.input: List curated skills and show which ones are installed.
output_examples.output: Skills from openai/skills: skill-a; skill-b, already installed. Which skill should be installed?

output_examples.input: Install the reviewed skill named skill-a.
output_examples.output: Installed skill-a in the configured Codex skills directory. Restart Codex to load the new skill.

best_practices: Review each repository and use an immutable commit before installation.
Use least-privilege credentials and keep tokens outside prompts and logs.
Confirm the destination, then restart Codex after a successful installation.
anti_patterns: Do not install skills from unknown repositories or mutable refs without review.
Do not expose GitHub tokens in prompts, command output, or shared logs.
Do not overwrite preinstalled system skills through routine installation workflows.

faq.question: Which sources does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports the OpenAI curated collection and user-provided GitHub repository paths.

faq.question: Can it install from private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Private access can use existing Git credentials or optional GitHub token environment variables.

faq.question: Can it install multiple skills?
faq.answer: Yes. The installer accepts multiple repository paths in one request.

faq.question: When does an installed skill become available?
faq.answer: Restart Codex after installation so the new skill can be loaded.

faq.question: Does the skill verify downloaded content?
faq.answer: No. Review the repository, pin an immutable commit, and verify content before installation.
